title.en: Comparing fractions and fractions greater than 1

text.en: Sevi and Shami share a chikki. Sevi eats 1/3 and Shami eats the rest, 2/3. Who ate more? And when Raman's dad cuts parathas into halves, Maa eats 5 halves - how many parathas is that?

When the denominators are the same, the pieces are the same size, so the bigger numerator is the bigger fraction. 2/3 is more than 1/3, so Shami ate more.
Compare 7/8 and 3/8: both are eighths, 7 > 3, so 7/8 > 3/8. Also 3/5 < 4/5 and 5/10 > 3/10.
When the numerators are the same, look at the pieces. 1/5 is bigger than 1/6, because fewer equal parts means bigger pieces. So 4/5 > 4/6 and 3/7 > 3/8.
Use the fraction kit to check: lay four 1/5 pieces and four 1/6 pieces side by side; the fifths strip is longer.
Now fractions greater than 1. Raman's father cuts each paratha into 2 halves. Maa eats 5 pieces of 1/2 = 5/2 parathas.
2 halves make 1 whole. 5 halves = 2 wholes + 1 half = 2 1/2 parathas. On a number line, 5/2 lies halfway between 2 and 3.
A fraction whose numerator is greater than its denominator is more than 1. 7/4 = 4/4 + 3/4 = 1 3/4. A number like 2 1/2 with a whole part and a fraction part is a mixed number.
To compare with 1: if numerator is smaller than the denominator, the fraction is less than 1 (3/4 < 1); if equal it is 1 (4/4); if greater it is more than 1 (5/4 > 1).

problem.en: Maa ate 5 pieces of 1/2 paratha. How many parathas did she eat?

why.en: Each piece is one half, so five of them make five halves.

text.en: 2 halves = 1 paratha, so 4 halves = 2 parathas, with 1 half left: 2 1/2 parathas.

why.en: Divide 5 by 2: quotient 2 is the whole part, remainder 1 is the numerator.

prompt.en: Which is greater, 3/7 or 3/8? Explain with a picture in your mind.

requiredIdeas.en: Same numerator, so compare the sizes of pieces

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking a bigger denominator means a bigger fraction

points.en: Same denominator: the bigger numerator is bigger.
Same numerator: the smaller denominator is bigger.
Fractions with numerator greater than denominator are more than 1 and can be written as mixed numbers: 5/2 = 2 1/2.
Compare any fraction with 1 using numerator and denominator.
